transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2025-12-17 15:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Lina Gomez (CSM), Ethan Zhao (SE) -- Maya Chen (Horizon), Liam O'Connor (Platform), Priya Singh (VP Product)

Summary:
Quick QBR to review usage, cost trends, reliability incidents in Q4, and align on roadmap for Dedicated / Private deployment evaluation. Agreed next steps around cost breakdown, reliability benchmarks, and security docs.

Transcript:
00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is jordan from Redwood, we've got lina and ethan with me. how's everyone doing?
00:06 Maya: good thanks, hey jordan, thanks for setting this up. busy quarter but excited to sync.
00:12 Jordan: great. quick agenda, usage and cost review, reliability incidents, product roadmap items relevant to horizon, and then next steps. sound good?
00:20 Priya: yep perfect.
00:24 Jordan: okay starting with usage - lina?
00:27 Lina: yeah, so month-over-month your token volume grew about 18% and that lines up with the new checkout assistant rollout. most of the increase is in generation traffic, embeddings are stable. the spike on 12/03 corresponded to the A/B test. we pulled the detailed per-route numbers into the sheet i shared.
00:45 Liam: that matches our telemetry. one question: costs are higher than we expected — any explanation?
00:50 Lina: right so the cost delta is two parts: higher token usage and tail latency causing more billing windows on the hosted plan; also you have a few long-sequence calls hitting 8k tokens which push the billing per request. jordan, maybe ethan can explain the latency effect quickly?
01:10 Ethan: sure — with our hosted API we price per token but long sequences and lower batching efficiency increase per-token cost. also if KV cache misses happen on cold starts you see more work per request. note the model variant you're on has a slightly higher per-token compute cost compared to the smaller quantized variant.
01:28 Maya: are we seeing caching misconfiguration? we thought prefix caching was enabled.
01:33 Ethan: from logs there were intermittent prefix cache misses during your busiest window, likely from frequent model restarts during their deploys. also some requests bypassed caching due to inconsistent conversation IDs from your front end. small SDK tweak there would help.
01:46 Liam: ok we'll look into consistent conv IDs — good to know. more broadly we want predictability; the finance team asked about committed capacity or reserved pricing.
01:54 Jordan: absolutely — that's where Redwood Dedicated comes in. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, and a rate card for committed usage. it also isolates your data. do you have timeline for procurement?
02:07 Priya: procurement wants a ballpark cost and SLA so they can budget. also security needs SOC2 and KMS info.
02:14 Jordan: we can send a templated commitment quote and SLA terms — lina will attach SOC 2 docs and a security pack. we also support customer-managed KMS for private deployments.
02:24 Priya: good. on latency, we saw a few incidents last month where 99th percentile spiked — can you walk through mitigation options?
02:31 Ethan: yep — main levers are: 1) Dedicated to reduce noisy neighbor and cold start variance; 2) quantized model variants to reduce compute and tail latency; 3) prefix/KV caching and session pinning to warm KV cache; 4) smart routing to another region or fallback smaller model during congestion. often a combination works best.
02:50 Maya: can we run a smoke demo of Dedicated with our traffic profile?
02:53 Jordan: yes we can do a proof-of-concept. ethan — can we scope a 24-hour reliability benchmark that mirrors horizon's traffic?
02:59 Ethan: yeah, i'll set up a run with the same seq length distribution and concurrency; i'll run with caching on and off and gather 50/95/99p latencies and token counts. i'll include logs and runtime metrics.
03:12 Liam: when you do the run, can you include a KV cache stress test and simulate rolling deploys? last time we saw restarts increase misses.
03:19 Ethan: noted. we'll simulate rolling restarts and include the impact on tail latency.
03:23 Priya: security — our compliance team asked specifically about audit logs, SSO/SAML, and RBAC. are these available in Dedicated or Private?
03:30 Lina: yes, Dedicated includes audit logs and SSO with SAML, and RBAC for console access. Private (VPC or on-prem) adds customer-managed KMS and more strict network controls. we'll share the security pack that outlines encryption in transit/at rest, KMS integration, and SOC 2 scope.
03:44 Maya: any gotchas with our regulatory stuff for EU data residency? some traffic is EU-only.
03:50 Jordan: we can route EU traffic to EU-hosted capacity and also support Private VPC in EMEA regions. for Dedicated we can provision capacity in the region you need.
03:59 Liam: region routing — is that automatic or do we need to set up rules?
04:03 Ethan: you can set routing policies by customer/route, or we can do per-request region hints. there are fallbacks too. we'll share a config sample.
04:12 Priya: one more question — how hard is migrating from hosted to Dedicated? downtime? code changes?
04:18 Ethan: low code changes if you keep the same API. main migration work is networking and routing rules plus updating auth keys. we usually do a canary cutover and run traffic split; zero-downtime is achievable with staged cutovers.
04:29 Jordan: quick recap of business value: Dedicated reduces cost per token for high volume, improves latency predictability, and gives better isolation which helps your security posture.
04:38 Maya: makes sense. we'll need a clear estimate of expected cost delta vs hosted so finance can sign off.
04:44 Lina: we'll include modeled scenarios: current hosted baseline, Dedicated with 30% commit, Dedicated with 60% commit — with per-route breakout.
04:52 Priya: timeline — we want to decide before end of Q1.
04:56 Jordan: good target. we'll push the PoC in December to give you data early.
05:00 (background cross-talk)
05:06 Ethan: small note — for your embedding pipelines, consider batching window tweaks and quantization. that shrinks cost a lot.
05:12 Liam: ok we'll review our jobs.
05:14 Maya: any risks to be aware of?
05:16 Ethan: biggest near-term risk is the conversation ID inconsistency causing cache misses; second is unoptimized long sequences; third is sudden traffic patterns that violate autoscale assumptions. the PoC will identify these.
05:29 Priya: action items?
05:31 Jordan: i'll list them: jordan sends cost breakdown and pricing scenarios; ethan runs 24-hour benchmark and shares logs; lina sends SOC2 and security pack; maya shares SRE contact and current incident runbook.
05:45 Maya: sounds good. thanks everyone.
05:48 Jordan: thanks all. we'll follow up with calendar invites for the PoC kickoff and price sheet.
05:54 End of call.
